title: In Silico Molecular Modeling of the Sodium Iodide Symporter from Homo sapiens
author: Hristina R. Zhekova

steps_raw.instruction: In Silico Molecular Modeling of the Sodium Iodide Symporter from Homo sapiens
Hristina R. Zhekova and Sergei Y. Noskov
Centre for Molecular Simulation, Department of Biological Sciences, University of Calgary, Calgary, Alberta, Canada
Multiple sequence alignment protocols

Alignments were made for NIS with respect to each of the available conformationally-relevant templates (6 templates with the LeuT-fold: LeuT1, AdiC2, BetP3, dDAT4, Mhp15, and vSGLT6). The multiple sequence alignments were performed with the align tool of Modeller 9.187, which overlaps the template crystal structures and uses structural information from this overlap to assign the amino acid sequences to helices and loops. To improve alignment in the ion/substrate binding domain of NIS, the putative sequences of TMs 1, 12, and 13 of NIS were removed and the remaining 5+5 fold of NIS (residues 50-439) was aligned with the 5+5 folds of the 6 selected templates. TMs 1 and 12 of NIS were modeled after TMs 1 and 12 of vSGLT (from PDB 2XQ28 and 3DH46, respectively), since the rest of the templates showed significant differences in this area. TM13 of NIS was excluded from modeling with the LeuT-fold templates due to poor sequence identity with all templates.
3D threading and refinement of the models

3D structures of NIS were built using the automodel function in Modeller 9.187 with alpha helical constraints imposed on residues 85-99, 279-296, 393-401, 409-425, 428-438 for better reproduction of the helical transmembrane domains. After assessment of similarities in the 3D structure of the 6 overlapped LeuT-fold templates they were divided in two groups: vSGLT-like (including vSGLT and Mhp1) and LeuT-like (including LeuT, AdiC, BetP, and dDAT). Three LeuT-fold models of NIS were generated afterwards: a vSGLT-like model based on vSGLT and Mhp1, a LeuT-like model based on LeuT, AdiC, BetP, and dDAT, and a mixed model based on all 6 templates. For each model, 500 structures were generated with Modeller 9.187, using automodel and the quality of the structures was assessed with pdfpdb7, DOPE9, and GA34110 scores. Afterwards, 5-10 structures with the lowest DOPE and highest GA341 scores were selected and overlapped with the templates for assessment of overall backbone structure and position of residues identified as important from experimental data (X-Ray diffraction where possible and functional mutagenesis). Selected structure were subjected to further side chain relaxation with ROSETTA MP.11
Side Chain Relaxation with ROSETTA

The NIS structures selected from the previous step were subjected to side-chain relaxation with the ROSETTA MP protocols11 in the presence of implicit membrane. The span files for the membrane were prepared manually with topology based on the initial 3D structures of NIS. 2000 decoy structures were generated for each of the 3 individual NIS models and were scored with the mpframework_smooth_fa_2012 function. The resultant structures were clustered with the cluster tool provided in ROSETTA. The center of the largest lowest energy cluster was chosen as a representative NIS model for the remaining GCMC and MD simulations.
